correctness.rationale: Every connected chordal graph admits a simplicial noncut vertex, yielding exhaustive clique-extension generation. All disconnected isomorphism types follow uniquely as component multisets. The verifier uses exact adjacency-preserving graph-isomorphism checks, common-palette 18-round color refinement (enough for all pairs of order ≤8), and checks every class from n1..8. Full result 2119 chordal n8 types, 2117 C2 classes, two nonsingleton pairs of size two; all counts independently agree with published enumerations; explicit pairs have matching equitable quotients but exact nonisomorphism. Computations are finite exhaustive, not generalized to n>8.

originality.rationale: Neither the class-relative split-graph nor the class-relative 2-tree first-collision theorem implies that all other chordal isomorphism types are separated by C2: those subclasses are proper and incomplete. The present exact census additionally quantifies across all 2119 chordal types and classifies their 2117 C2-equivalence classes, including the absence of other collisions. The two example pairs are explicitly acknowledged as prior examples. General amenability results and published counts do not state or entail this class-relative exhaustive logical result. Search is bounded and independent priority review remains pending.

value.rationale: A complete exact first-obstruction classification in a canonical hereditary graph class is natural and not supplied by the known 2-tree and split-graph existence witnesses. It establishes that all other chordal types through order eight are separated by counting logic and identifies two distinct structures for the only failures. This is a motivated structural boundary and a reproducible finite benchmark, not a mere renaming or arbitrary slice.
